what_it_means: The hit rate a bettor needs just to break even at the standard -110 price.
The joint hit rate a two-leg parlay needs to break even; independence cannot be assumed.
A break-even bettor looks like a 55% handicapper over 50 bets about 36% of the time - short samples are mostly luck.
Even over 200 bets, a break-even bettor still looks like 55% about 21% of the time.
Only at ~1000 bets does the false-55% probability fall below 5%.

metric: Bets needed to prove a true 55% edge (80% power)
what_it_means: How many bets it would take to distinguish a genuine 55% hit rate from break-even.

metric: Bets needed to prove a true 53% edge (80% power)
what_it_means: A 0.6-point true edge is effectively unprovable at practical sample sizes.
A 92.9% hit rate over 14 bets has a Wilson lower bound of 0.685 - the apparent skill is not established.
A failing signal (-27.4 pts vs break-even) still shows a positive bankroll because the largest stakes won; ranking on profit would have promoted it.
